questions.q: What incident prompts Overlook Medical Group's IT Director to question the backup plan?
options: A developer accidentally dropped a staging table on the shared database, and no one could say for certain it was recoverable
A ransomware attack encrypted the Patients table
The nightly maintenance plan job failed and sent an alert email
The Azure subscription ran out of storage quota
questions.explain: The scare was a developer's cleanup script dropping a staging table on the shared database — not a failure alert, which is exactly why it exposed that nobody actually knew if a real restore would work.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say a backup job reporting 'success' is not the same claim as 'this database can be recovered'?
options: Because a backup that has never been restored is an untested hypothesis, not a proven plan
Because maintenance plans only back up schema, never data
Because Azure SQL Database silently corrupts backups older than 24 hours
Because a successful backup job always means the restore will take longer than expected
questions.explain: The only way to know a backup actually works is to restore it. A green job history entry says the backup ran — it says nothing about whether a restore from it would succeed.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly scoped INTO this capstone project?
options: A custom automated alerting and monitoring pipeline
A full high-availability and geo-replication architecture
A company-wide backup audit across every Overlook system
One database, with backups explained, a tested point-in-time restore, a health check, and a short runbook
questions.explain: The project is deliberately scoped to one database with a real, tested, documented backup-and-restore plan — not a company-wide audit, HA architecture, or custom automation framework.

questions.q: What does 'recovery point objective (RPO)' mean, as defined in this lesson?
options: The number of years a backup must be retained for compliance
The total storage capacity reserved for backup files
How much data loss is acceptable, measured in time — it drives how often log backups run
The exact time of day the nightly maintenance plan is scheduled to run
questions.explain: RPO is about acceptable data loss measured in time, which is what determines how frequently you need to take transaction log backups.

questions.q: What is a 'runbook' in the context of this capstone?
options: The Azure Portal's automated deployment template for SQL resources
A script that automatically restores a database every night for testing
The T-SQL job history stored in msdb
A written, step-by-step plan a team member could follow during a real incident without the original author present
questions.explain: A runbook is the written plan — Lesson 9's deliverable — that lets the backup-and-restore plan survive beyond one person's memory.
